draft.headline: Tech drags Nasdaq futures lower even as bond yields fall
draft.summary: Nasdaq futures are down 1.23% before the open, far more than the S&P 500. Headlines point to Alphabet and AI-spending worries. Yields fell, which usually helps tech, but company news looks like the bigger force today.
draft.what_it_means: Jobless claims came in at 194K, below the 198K forecast. Fewer people filing for unemployment means the job market is holding up. Last week's figure was revised up by 1K to 195K. There is not enough history to say whether this surprise was big. Core PCE, the Fed's favourite inflation gauge, and GDP are not in our data yet. One headline says GDP grew a better-than-expected 3.4% and September inflation accelerated. Treat that as unconfirmed until the official figures arrive.
draft.market_reaction: In the 15 minutes after 08:30, NQ slipped 0.13% and the S&P 500 0.05%, a small move. Today NQ is down 1.23% to 29,611.75, below yesterday's low of 29,680.75. Headlines say Alphabet faces a record post-earnings loss and that Google and Microsoft held off raising AI spending forecasts. The session's range is already 62% of a typical day. Oil fell 1.44% to $101.30. The dollar rose 0.10%.
draft.rates_read: The 2-year yield fell 4.4bp to 4.691%. The 10-year fell 4.0bp to 5.005%. That includes drops of 2.7bp and 1.9bp in the 15 minutes after the 08:30 data. Lower yields usually help Nasdaq stocks. NQ falling anyway suggests company news, not rates, is driving today. The 10-year is still just above 5%, a high level that makes future tech profits worth less today.

draft.learn: The VXN is the Nasdaq 'fear gauge'. It shows how much movement options traders expect. It closed Wednesday at 23.78, well above the VIX at 16.97. When VXN sits above VIX, traders worry more about tech than the wider market. That fits a day when tech is leading the losses.
